steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 170C. Line a tin.
Melt {{ing:butter-block}}, {{ing:golden-syrup}} and {{ing:sugar-soft-brown}} in a pan.
Stir until the sugar has dissolved.
Take off the heat. Stir in {{ing:oats-rolled}}.
Press into the tin firmly.
steps.note: Loose flapjack crumbles when you cut it.

steps.instruction: Bake 25 minutes, until golden at the edges.
Cut into squares while warm. Cool in the tin.

swaps.text: A dairy-free block or spread, or olive oil where it is only for frying, to make it dairy free

steps.instruction: Blitz {{ing:dates-pitted}} until they form a paste.
Add {{ing:oats-rolled}}, {{ing:peanut-butter}} and {{ing:cocoa-powder}}.
Blitz again until it holds together when pressed.
Roll into balls the size of a walnut.
Roll them in {{ing:desiccated-coconut}}.
Chill 30 minutes before eating.

swaps.text: Oats labelled gluten free
Sunflower seed butter, for a nut-free version

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 160C.
Chop {{ing:almonds}} roughly.
Mix {{ing:oats-rolled}}, the almonds, {{ing:pumpkin-seeds}} and {{ing:cinnamon-ground}}.
Warm {{ing:honey}} and {{ing:vegetable-oil}} together in a pan.
Pour over the oats and stir until coated.
Spread on a tray. Bake 25 minutes, stirring twice.
Stir in {{ing:raisins}} after it comes out.
steps.note: Raisins burn if they go in the oven.

steps.instruction: Cool completely before storing.

steps.instruction: Line a small tin.
Warm {{ing:peanut-butter}} and {{ing:honey}} in a pan until loose.
Take off the heat. Stir in {{ing:oats-rolled}} and {{ing:sunflower-seeds}}.
Press firmly into the tin.
Melt {{ing:dark-chocolate}} in a bowl over hot water.
Pour it over and spread flat.
Chill 2 hours, then cut into bars.

steps.instruction: Slice {{ing:cheddar-cheese}} and {{ing:apple-medium}}.
Put them on a plate with {{ing:walnuts}}.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 180C. Line a muffin tin.
Mash {{ing:banana-medium}} in a bowl.
Beat in {{ing:egg-medium}}, {{ing:vegetable-oil}} and {{ing:sugar-soft-brown}}.
Stir in {{ing:flour-self-raising}}, {{ing:oats-rolled}} and {{ing:cinnamon-ground}}.
Stop stirring as soon as it comes together.
Spoon into the tin. Bake 22 minutes.
A skewer should come out clean.

recipes.name: Crispy roast chickpeas
recipes.method_note: Dry them well. Wet chickpeas steam instead of crisping.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 200C.
Drain and rinse {{ing:chickpeas-tinned}}. Pat dry with kitchen roll.
Toss on a baking tray with {{ing:olive-oil}}, {{ing:paprika}}, {{ing:cumin-ground}} and {{ing:salt}}.
Roast for 30 minutes, until crunchy. Shake the tray halfway.
Cool for 5 minutes on the tray.
steps.note: They crisp up more as they cool.

recipes.name: Salted edamame
recipes.method_note: Eat the beans and leave the pods.

steps.instruction: Boil a pan of water.
Add {{ing:edamame-frozen}}. Cook for 4 minutes, until bright green.
Drain well.
Toss with {{ing:salt}} and a squeeze of {{ing:lime}}.

recipes.name: Apple and peanut butter stacks
recipes.method_note: Use almond butter or sunflower seed butter if peanuts are a problem.

steps.instruction: Core {{ing:apple-medium}}. Slice into rings about as thick as a coin.
Spread each ring with some of {{ing:peanut-butter}}.
Scatter over {{ing:raisins}} and {{ing:sunflower-seeds}}.

swaps.text: Sunflower seed butter, for a nut-free version

recipes.name: Two-banana oat cookies
recipes.method_note: Spotty bananas are sweetest. These are soft, not crunchy.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 180C. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Mash {{ing:banana-medium}} in a bowl with a fork.
Stir in {{ing:oats-rolled}}, {{ing:raisins}}, {{ing:cinnamon-ground}} and {{ing:peanut-butter}}.
Roll into 12 balls. Flatten each on the tray.
Bake for 15 minutes, until golden at the edges.
Cool on the tray for 10 minutes before moving.
steps.note: They firm up as they cool.

Sunflower seed butter, for a nut-free version

recipes.name: Veg sticks and hummus
recipes.method_note: Cut a batch on Sunday. Kept in water in the fridge, they stay crunchy for three days.

steps.instruction: Peel {{ing:carrot-medium}}. Cut into sticks.
Cut {{ing:cucumber}} and {{ing:pepper-bell}} into sticks.
Spoon {{ing:hummus}} into a bowl. Sprinkle with {{ing:paprika}}.

recipes.name: Sardines and tomato on toast
recipes.method_note: Cheap, filling and full of omega-3. The bones are soft enough to eat.

steps.instruction: Toast {{ing:wholemeal-bread-slice}}.
Halve {{ing:cherry-tomato}}. Put them on the toast.
Drain {{ing:sardines-tinned}}. Lay them over the tomatoes.
Squeeze over {{ing:lemon}}. Sprinkle with {{ing:chilli-powder}}.

swaps.text: Gluten-free bread

recipes.name: Chicken satay bites
recipes.method_note: Make a double batch of sauce. It keeps a week in the fridge and goes with noodles.

steps.instruction: Cut {{ing:chicken-breast-skinless}} into bite-sized pieces.
Toss with half of {{ing:soy-sauce}} and {{ing:curry-powder}}.
Heat {{ing:vegetable-oil}} in a frying pan on a medium-high heat.
Fry the chicken 8 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through.
Warm {{ing:peanut-butter}}, {{ing:coconut-milk-tinned}} and {{ing:honey}} in a small pan, stirring.
Stir in the rest of the soy sauce and the juice of {{ing:lime}}.
Serve the chicken on cocktail sticks with the sauce for dipping.
